2027-01-19.title: Third Tuesday of Denha · Second Day of the Three Days' Fast
2027-01-19.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Return to the LORD with all your heart
Your iniquities have been barriers between you and your God
Be transformed by the renewing of your minds
The Pharisee and the tax collector
2027-01-19.alt: Season of Denha. Three Days' Fast (Moonnu Nombu, the Rogation of the Ninevites). Church Unity Octave.
2027-01-19.verse: But the tax collector, standing far off, would not even look up to heaven, but was beating his breast and saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’
theo: On the second day of the fast the readings show what a true fast looks like. At Mizpah Samuel tells Israel: “If you are returning to the LORD with all your heart, then put away the foreign gods”. The people draw water and pour it out before the LORD, fast all day and confess: “We have sinned against the LORD.” When the Philistines attack, they beg Samuel: “Do not cease to cry out to the LORD our God for us”, and Samuel prays, “and the LORD answered him.” Isaiah explains why prayer can seem unheard: “See, the LORD’s hand is not too short to save, nor his ear too dull to hear. Rather, your iniquities have been barriers between you and your God”. Fasting is the work of taking those barriers down.

Then Jesus shows two men at prayer. The Pharisee is a serious religious man: “I fast twice a week; I give a tenth of all my income.” But he prays “standing by himself”, comparing himself with “this tax collector”. The tax collector stands far off and says only: “God, be merciful to me, a sinner!” It is he who goes home justified, “for all who exalt themselves will be humbled, but all who humble themselves will be exalted.” Paul shows the fruit of such humility: we offer our bodies “as a living sacrifice”, we are “transformed by the renewing of your minds”, and we learn “not to think of yourself more highly than you ought to think”, because “we, who are many, are one body in Christ”. A fast that makes us proud is the Pharisee's fast; a fast that makes us humble and one with others is the fast God accepts. In this Unity Octave, the tax collector's prayer is also the prayer of divided Christians.
outline: Ask: can someone fast, pray and give to the Church, and still go home without God's mercy?
Point 1 · Return with all your heart
Mizpah: idols put away, water poured out, sin confessed.
God's hand is not too short; our sins stand in between.
The proud fast and the humble prayer.
“God, be merciful to me, a sinner!”
live: Repeat it slowly throughout the day, especially when you feel hungry.
Remove one thing that stands between you and God: an app, a habit, a resentment.
2027-01-19.prayer: Lord God, your hand is not too short to save. Take away the barriers our sins have raised between us and you. Keep us from the pride that fasts and despises others; give us the heart of the tax collector, and transform us by the renewing of our minds, one body in Christ. God, be merciful to us, sinners. Amen.
altar: At the beginning of the Holy Qurbana we confess that we are sinners and ask for mercy. We come like the tax collector, and offer ourselves with Christ as a living sacrifice.

quick: Return to God with all your heart and put away idols.
Our sins are the barrier, not God's weakness.
The humble tax collector, not the proud Pharisee, goes home justified.
2027-01-19.action: Repeat the tax collector's prayer throughout the day.
2027-01-19.question: Does my fasting make me humbler, or does it make me compare myself with others?

family.explain: Two men went to pray. One said: God, I am better than others! The other said: God, be merciful to me, a sinner. Jesus said the second man pleased God.
family.intention: We pray for people who feel far from God, and for ourselves, that we may be humble.
family.ask: Ask: “Let us all say together slowly: God, be merciful to me, a sinner.”

illus: A church trustee in Thrissur had kept every fast for forty years and told everyone so. During one Moonnu Nombu his grandson asked him why he always sat in the front pew while old Kunjamma sat near the door. The question stayed with him. The next day he sat at the back beside her, and found that for the first time he prayed: God, be merciful to me, a sinner.

pm.open: Lord God, your hand is not too short to save. Remove the barriers between us and you, and make us humble. Amen.
share: If you are returning to the LORD with all your heart, put away the foreign gods (1 Samuel 7:3). What idol must I put away?
Your iniquities have been barriers between you and your God (Isaiah 59:2). What stands between me and God?
God, be merciful to me, a sinner! (Luke 18:13). Do I pray like the Pharisee or like the tax collector?
pm.resp: God, be merciful to us, sinners.
interc: For the Church, that her fasting may be humble and sincere.
For those who despise others and those who are despised.
For all who feel their prayers are unheard.
For the unity of Christians, one body in Christ.
For our group, that we may be transformed by the renewing of our minds.
pm.close: Father, you lift up the humble. Accept our fast and our prayer, take away our sins, and make us one body in Christ. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, on this second day of the fast, the readings ask: what kind of fast pleases God? At Mizpah Samuel tells Israel: if you are returning to the LORD with all your heart, put away the foreign gods (1 Samuel 7:3). The people pour out water before the LORD, fast and confess: we have sinned against the LORD. Samuel prays for them, and the LORD answers.

Isaiah answers those who complain that God does not hear: the LORD's hand is not too short to save, nor his ear too dull to hear. Rather, your iniquities have been barriers between you and your God (Isaiah 59:1–2). Fasting is the work of taking down those barriers, stone by stone.

Then Jesus tells of two men at prayer. The Pharisee fasts twice a week and gives a tenth of all his income. But his prayer is about himself, and he despises the tax collector. The tax collector stands far off, beats his breast and says: God, be merciful to me, a sinner (Luke 18:13). Jesus says this man went home justified.

Notice: the Pharisee fasted. Fasting is not the problem. Pride is the problem. Paul tells us not to think of ourselves more highly than we ought, because we, who are many, are one body in Christ (Romans 12:3, 5). A fast that makes us look down on others has missed its goal.
In this Unity Octave, let us pray the tax collector's prayer for ourselves and for all Christians. God, be merciful to us, sinners, and make us one. Amen.
kids: Children, one man said to God: I am so good! Another man said: God, be merciful to me, a sinner. Jesus liked the second prayer. Let us pray it today: Jesus, have mercy on me.

intro: Theme: “God, be merciful to me, a sinner!”
The fast God accepts: a whole heart, walls taken down, a humble prayer.

q: If you are returning to the LORD with all your heart, then put away the foreign gods and the Astartes from among you. Direct your heart to the LORD, and serve him only,
Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded.
points.apply: Put away one idol during the fast.

q: See, the LORD’s hand is not too short to save, nor his ear too dull to hear. Rather, your iniquities have been barriers between you and your God, and your sins have hidden his face from you so that he does not hear.
Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your minds, so that you may discern what is the will of God
points.apply: Examine your conscience tonight and name the barriers.

q: The sacrifice acceptable to God is a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.
I tell you, this man went down to his home justified rather than the other; for all who exalt themselves will be humbled, but all who humble themselves will be exalted.
points.apply: Pray the tax collector's prayer many times today.

concl: Fasting takes down the walls our sins have built.
The fast God accepts is humble and unites us with others.
2027-01-19.resolve: Do not speak of your fasting to anyone this week; speak only to God.
